subject: Throughput degradation and contract offset request
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@duraflow.io>
To: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production throughput spikes — impact and next steps

Hi David and Laura,

We ran into another throughput degradation window this morning between 02:30–03:40 UTC; our ingestion pipeline backpressure spiked and a number of jobs failed retries. This is a repeat of the pattern we've seen three times in the last 30 days and it's directly impacting batch SLAs with our downstream ETL consumers.

I've attached a short CSV with the token/service-level metrics for the incident (duraflow_throughput_July14.csv). To be explicit about asks:
- We need a remediation plan and timeline that prevents recurrence.
- We are requesting a commercial offset for the impacted periods while we evaluate long-term mitigations.

Sandra (CFO) is copied — she asked that we quantify the dollar impact and start the contractual conversation now.

Can we get an executive touchpoint today?

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering
Duraflow Systems

Subject: Re: Production throughput spikes — impact and next steps

Alex — thanks for the flag and for the data. I’m sorry about the recurrence; we take these regressions very seriously.

Immediate next steps I can commit to today:
- Executive call at 3pm PT (I’ll send invite) to surface ops root cause and commercial options.
- Short-term mitigation: we can provision a dedicated burst pool for your critical ingestion routes for the next 14 days to remove noisy neighbor interference while we fix the underlying cause.
- Preliminary commercial offer: a credit equal to 10% of your July invoice for the impacted days, plus eight hours of engineering time for tuning. This is preliminary — we’ll confirm after the analysis.

Laura/Rishi/Grace — please prepare an initial incident postmortem and a cost estimate for the dedicated burst plan. Link any quick analysis artifacts to the exec invite.

Alex — I’ll follow up in the call with a DocuSign amendment we can sign for the immediate offset + burst pool.

-David
David Kim
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

To: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production throughput spikes — impact and next steps

Team — quick analysis attached (redwood_analysis_duraflow_q3.xlsx). Highlights:
- Root cause: transient autoscaling lag plus a KV cache eviction pattern on the specific model route used by Duraflow's ingestion (region-us-west-2).
- Impact window calculation: 3 incidents, total 4.5 hours of elevated 95p latency and ~2.7M additional tokens processed at >2x cost profile.
- Preliminary credit calculation: 10% of July MRR prorated for incident hours ≈ $22,000.
- Remediation plan: immediate dedicated burst pool + prioritized kernel pinning for the route (7–10 day work), plus a follow-up latency regression test harness.

I recommend we:
1) Offer the credit above as a one-off for July,
2) Provide two months of free burst pool for the critical ingestion route (to match their operational window),
3) Amend the SLA language to add an explicit escalation path and a performance-runbook for throughput-sensitive routes.

If we agree, I can draft the amendment language.

-Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Formal offer: July offset + operational remediation timeline

Alex / Sandra — following our call and the internal analysis, here’s Redwood’s formal offer for the incidents covering the July windows:

1) Commercial offset: a one-time credit equal to 10% of your July invoice covering the prorated incident hours (estimated credit $22,000).
2) Platform relief: immediate provisioning of a dedicated burst pool for your ingestion routes for two months at no charge (we’ll schedule provisioning within 24 hours of the amendment being signed).
3) Operational commitments: a technical remediation plan with milestone checkpoints — kernel pinning + cache policy adjustments (ETA 7–10 business days), and a post-remediation load test with your team.
4) Contract: we’ll deliver a short contract amendment that documents the credit, the burst pool terms, and an updated escalation clause. The amendment will be sent via DocuSign for signature: https://docusign.net/sign/0ABC123456789

If the above is acceptable, we can route the amendment through your legal team and provision the burst pool immediately after signature.

I appreciate your patience and will own the delivery. If you’d prefer a different commercial structure (e.g., fixed dollar credit vs percent), let me know — we’re flexible to expedite resolution.

-David Kim
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

David — thank you. The proposal looks reasonable to Duraflow leadership. We accept the 10% credit and the two-month burst pool, and we appreciate the remediation timeline.

Two quick asks before signature:
- Can you include an explicit clause that the burst pool will not be used to throttle other committed capacity (clarify isolation)?
- We’d like a 30-minute handoff call after provisioning to walk our infra team through the new route config and failover steps.

Sandra will route the amendment to legal; once we have the signed DocuSign, please provision the burst pool and schedule the handoff.

Appreciate the quick work here.

—Alex

Duraflow Systems
